paper.title: On Sample Complexity Upper and Lower Bounds for Exact Ranking from Noisy Comparisons

settings.name_in_paper: Exact ranking from pairwise comparisons (assumptions A1-A3)
unmapped: Goal is to recover the full exact ranking of n items with probability >= 1-delta (delta-correct)
Assumptions: independent comparisons, unique true ranking, weak stochastic transitivity (i > j iff p_ij > 1/2); no knowledge of gaps
unique_optimal_arm used to express the unique total ranking assumption A2
settings.definition_quote: Given $\delta\in(0,1/2)$ and $n$ items, one wants to determine the true ranking with probability at least $1-\delta$ by adaptively choosing sets of items to compare.

settings.name_in_paper: Exact ranking under the MNL model, pairwise comparisons (lower bound)
unmapped: Comparisons follow the multinomial logit (BTL/Plackett-Luce) model p_{i,S} = theta_i / sum_{j in S} theta_j; learner knows the model is MNL
Goal: exact full ranking with probability >= 1-delta
settings.definition_quote: each item $i$ holds a parameter $\gamma_i\in \mathbb{R}$ such that for any set $S$ containing $i$, $p_{i,S}=\exp(\gamma_i)/\sum_{j\in S}\exp(\gamma_j)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Exact ranking under the MNL model, listwise (m-wise) comparisons (lower bound)
unmapped: Listwise (multi-item) comparisons of any size m in {2,...,n} returning a noisy winner under MNL
Goal: exact full ranking with probability >= 1-delta
settings.definition_quote: to correctly rank these $n$ items with probability $1-\delta$, even with $m$-wise comparisons for all $m\in\{2,3,...,n\}$

unmapped: m-wise comparisons that return the most preferred item w.h.p. (essentially noiseless)
settings.definition_quote: If all comparisons are correct w.h.p., to exactly rank $n$ items w.h.p. by using $m$-wise comparisons, $\Theta(n\log_m{n})$ comparisons are needed.

symbols.Dt_i: tilde Delta_i = min |p_{i,j}-1/2| over items j adjacent to i in the true ranking
symbols.M_x: min{ sum_i Dt_i^{-2} log(1/x_i) : sum_i x_i <= 1 } (implies an n log n-type term)

conditions: algorithm is delta-correct for all instances satisfying A1-A3 and has no prior knowledge of the gaps

source.label: Theorem:LB
source.quote: Given $\delta\in(0,1/12)$ and an instance $\mathcal{I}$ with $n$ items, then the number of comparisons used by a $\delta$-correct algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ with no prior knowledge about the gaps of $\mathcal{I}$ is lower bounded by \tilde{\Omega}(...loglog...) + \Omega(... log(1/delta) + min{...}).

results.notes: Mixed notation: the loglog term is tilde-Omega (paper's Definition 1, 'almost Omega'), the other terms are Omega. Recorded as Omega_tilde overall. Number 'Theorem 1' assumed from shared counter being first theorem; label given.

bound.regime: delta <= 1/poly(n), or max_{i,j} Dt_i/Dt_j <= O(n^{1/2-p}) for some constant p>0

symbols.Dt_i: tilde Delta_i = min |p_{i,j}-1/2| over items j adjacent to i in the true ranking

conditions: delta-correct algorithm with no prior knowledge of the gaps

source.label: Theorem:LB
source.quote: If $\delta \preceq 1/poly(n)$, or $\max_{i,j\in[n]}\{\tilde{\Delta}_i/\tilde{\Delta}_j\} \preceq n^{1/2-p}$ for some constant $p>0$, then the lower bound becomes \tilde{\Omega}\big(\sum_{i\in[n]}\tilde{\Delta}_i^{-2}\log\log\tilde{\Delta}_i^{-1}\big) + \Omega \big(\sum_{i\in[n]}\tilde{\Delta}_i^{-2}\log(n/\delta)\big).

results.notes: n = K. Tight under SST (matches IIR upper bound).

symbols.Dp_i: min_{j != i} |p_{i,j} - 1/2| (equals tilde Delta_i under MNL)
symbols.M_x: min{ sum_i Dp_i^{-2} log(1/x_i) : sum_i x_i <= 1 }

conditions: delta-correct algorithm knowing instances follow the MNL model

source.label: Theorem:LBMNL
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1/12)$ and given a $\delta$-correct algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ with the knowledge that the input instances satisfy the MNL model, let $N_\mathcal{A}$ be the number of comparisons conducted by $\mathcal{A}$, then $\mathbb{E}[N_\mathcal{A}]$ is lower bounded by Eq. (\ref{Eq:GLB}) with a (possibly) different hidden constant factor.

bound.regime: delta <= 1/poly(n), or max_{i,j} Dp_i/Dp_j <= O(n^{1/2-p}) for some constant p>0

symbols.Dp_i: min_{j != i} |p_{i,j} - 1/2| (equals tilde Delta_i under MNL)

conditions: delta-correct algorithm knowing the MNL model

source.label: Theorem:LBMNL
source.quote: When $\delta \preceq 1/poly(n)$ or $\max_{i,j\in[n]}\{\Delta_i/\Delta_j\} \preceq n^{1/2-p}$ for some constant $p>0$, the sample complexity is lower bounded by Eq. (\ref{Eq:LB}) with a (possibly) different hidden constant factor.

symbols.M_x: min{ sum_i Dp_i^{-2} log(1/x_i) : sum_i x_i <= 1 }

conditions: delta-correct algorithm, MNL model, m-wise comparisons allowed for all m in {2,...,n}

source.label: Theorem:LBLWMNL
source.quote: Under the MNL model, given $n$ items with preference scores $\theta_1,\theta_2,...,\theta_n$ ..., to correctly rank these $n$ items with probability $1-\delta$, even with $m$-wise comparisons for all $m\in\{2,3,...,n\}$, the lower bound is the same as the pairwise ranking (i.e., Theorem~\ref{Theorem:LBMNL}) with (possibly) different hidden constant factors.

results.notes: Also the Eq. (LB) form holds under the same regime conditions as Theorem LBMNL (expression sum Dp_i^-2 (loglog(1/Dp_i) + log(n/delta))).

source.label: Proposition:HPC
source.quote: If all comparisons are correct w.h.p., to exactly rank $n$ items w.h.p. by using $m$-wise comparisons, $\Theta(n\log_m{n})$ comparisons are needed.

results.notes: Lower bound via Fano's inequality on expected number of comparisons.

source.label: Proposition:HPC
source.quote: If all comparisons are correct w.h.p., to exactly rank $n$ items w.h.p. by using $m$-wise comparisons, $\Theta(n\log_m{n})$ comparisons are needed.

results.notes: Upper bound achieved by LWMS (Lemma 4: 'Algorithm LWMS correctly ranks n items with high probability using O(n log_m n) comparisons'); deterministic count.

source.label: Theorem:TP-IIR
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, IIR returns the exact ranking of $[n]$, and conducts at most $O(\sum_{i\in[n]}{{\Delta_i^{-2}}(\log\log{\Delta_i^{-1}}+\log({n}/\delta))})$ comparisons.

results.notes: Requires no knowledge of gaps. Matches lower bound under SST (Delta_i = tilde Delta_i) and mild conditions.
